body: Cannot reproduce, need way more information.

This bug happens to me now too. Here some information to our infrastructure hope this helps: We are using a Rails App with Devise in place to handle session handling with plain Rails Views. After login we are redirect the user to an index page which starts an Marionette App. And then the dashboard should appear. Some it looks it never lets the requests finish see Screenshots attached. Besides our own assets we are loading external libs like - mixpanel - google ads - usersnap - braintree - tinymce But it seems to make no difference. I'm happy to a screensharing session if that helps to debug things. Update: Issue for me in version 0.17.5 present too. In 0.17.4 is not happening.

I was able to reproduce this with the following:

test:

```js
cy.visit('with-form.html')
cy.get('form').submit()
```

with-form.html:

```html
<iframe src="http://example.com"></iframe>
<form action="redirected-to.html"></form>
```

redirected-to.html:

```html
<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-2.2.3.min.js" integrity="sha256-a23g1Nt4dtEYOj7bR+vTu7+T8VP13humZFBJNIYoEJo=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
<script>
  $.get('/cypress.json')
  $.get('/cypress.json')
  $.get('/cypress.json')
  $.get('/cypress.json')
</script>
```

The key seems to be having an iframe on the first page (doesn't have to be cross-domain), having the page redirect through some action (like a form submit), and then having the page it redirects to fire off a bunch of XHR requests. 

The above case will sometimes not throw the error, since the error is caused by a race condition (discussed below) that doesn't always trigger.

The error itself `Cannot read property 'opener'...` comes from jQuery, and jQuery has added a guard against that since version 3.0.0. We currently use jQuery 2.1.4, but upgrading may not necessarily be the solution. 

The real issue is a race condition when snapshotting a page that gets redirected. We try to get the dimensions of any iframes on the page, so they can be replaced with placeholders in the snapshot. If we run into that race condition, the original document for the snapshot is gone, so jQuery gets thrown off when trying to get the iframe's dimensions. We probably need to account for that and be more resilient in case of such a race condition.

Yay, we literally spent hours trying to reproduce and finally its obvious.

The XHR stuff is incidental - the problem here is that if we try to snapshot **before** any `<iframe>` has actually been loaded then the `document` and `window` of that `<iframe>` is `null` which then causes jquery to fail deep inside its code.

The fix is simple - if `window` or `document` is not available then just skip replacing this iframe because its as if it doesn't exist, it displaces no client height or width and its essentially meaningless.

Okay I am wrong, the real root cause isn't that the `document` and `window` properties aren't available - they aren't available because Cypress is still holding a reference **to the old** app page, prior to page load. 

Since those elements are long gone, the browser throws a fit trying to access them.

Cypress normally updates `document` and `window` references on the `load` event, but because these XHR's are happening prior to that, we see this behavior.

What we need to do is hook into `onBeforeLoad` and update the references immediately since page events happening before load can cause snapshots.
thanks for the quick fixes, helped me so much
